nodes.summary: The Mahler measure of Lehmer's polynomial is at most $1176281/1000000 = 1.176281$.
nodes.title: Mahler measure of Lehmer's polynomial

nodes.summary: For every integer $a$, the Mahler measure of the integer polynomial $X - a$ is $\max(1, |a|)$.
nodes.title: Mahler measure of a monic linear integer polynomial

nodes.summary: The integer polynomial $X - 1$ has Mahler measure $1$.
nodes.title: Mahler measure of $X - 1$

nodes.summary: The integer polynomial $X - 2$ has Mahler measure $2$.
nodes.title: Mahler measure of $X - 2$

nodes.summary: The Mahler measure of $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is the Mahler measure of its image in $\mathbb{C}[X]$. It equals $|a| \prod_i \max(1, |\alpha_i|)$, where $a$ is the leading coefficient of $f$ and the $\alpha_i$ are the complex roots of $f$ counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Mahler measure of an integer polynomial

nodes.summary: An integer polynomial $f$ is reciprocal when reversing its coefficients gives $f$ or $-f$, that is, when $X^d f(1/X) = f$ or $X^d f(1/X) = -f$, where $d$ is the degree of $f$, taken to be $0$ when $f = 0$.
nodes.title: Reciprocal polynomial

nodes.summary: Lehmer's constant equals $1$ if and only if Lehmer's question has a positive answer, that is, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is an integer polynomial whose Mahler measure lies strictly between $1$ and $1 + \varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Lehmer's question in terms of Lehmer's constant

nodes.summary: For every integer polynomial $f$ whose Mahler measure is strictly larger than $1$, Lehmer's constant is at most the Mahler measure of $f$.
nodes.title: Lehmer's constant bounds every Mahler measure above $1$

nodes.summary: Writing $M(f)$ for the Mahler measure of an integer polynomial $f$, Lehmer's constant is $C_{40a} = \inf \{M(f) : f \in \mathbb{Z}[X],\ M(f) > 1\}$, the infimum of the Mahler measures of integer polynomials that are strictly larger than $1$.
nodes.title: Lehmer's constant

nodes.summary: Lehmer's polynomial is the integer polynomial $X^{10} + X^9 - X^7 - X^6 - X^5 - X^4 - X^3 + X + 1$.
nodes.title: Lehmer's polynomial

nodes.summary: The proposition that there are integer polynomials with Mahler measure arbitrarily close to $1$ from above: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ whose Mahler measure $M(f)$ satisfies $1 < M(f) < 1 + \varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Lehmer's question
Lehmer's upper bound for Lehmer's constant

nodes.summary: This is the set of real numbers of the form $M(f)$, where $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is an integer polynomial whose Mahler measure $M(f)$ is strictly larger than $1$.
nodes.title: Mahler measures above one

nodes.summary: If $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is a nonzero polynomial, then its Mahler measure satisfies $M(f) \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Nonzero integer polynomials have Mahler measure at least one

nodes.summary: Lehmer's constant $L$, the infimum of the Mahler measures strictly larger than $1$ of polynomials in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$, satisfies $1 \le L$.
nodes.title: Lehmer's constant is at least one

nodes.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be an integer polynomial that is not reciprocal and whose constant term $f(0)$ is nonzero. Then the Mahler measure of $f$ is at least the Mahler measure of Smyth's polynomial $X^3 - X - 1$.
nodes.title: Smyth's theorem for nonreciprocal polynomials

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
